old_text: A run is scored :— 1st—So often as the Batsmen, after a hit, or at any time while the ball is in play, shall have crossed, and made good their ground from end to end. 2nd—For penalties under Laws 16, 34, 41, and allowances under 44.
new_text: A run is scored:— 1st—So often as the Batsmen, after a hit, or at any time while the ball is in play, shall have crossed, and made good their ground from end to end. 2nd—For penalties under Laws 16, 34, 41, and allowances under 44.

old_text: The stumps shall be of equal and of sufficient size to prevent the ball from passing through, twenty-seven inches out of the ground.
new_text: The stumps shall be of equal and of sufficient size to prevent the bail from passing through, twenty-seven inches out of the ground.

old_text: The Bowling Crease shall be in a line with the stumps: eight feet eight inches in length; the stumps in the centre; with a Return Crease at each end, at right angles behind the wicket.
new_text: The bowling crease shall be in a line with the stumps; eight feet eight inches in length; the stumps in the centre; with a Return Crease at each end, at right angles behind the wicket.

old_text: The Ball must be bowled; if thrown or jerked either Umpires shall call “No Ball.”
new_text: The Ball must be bowled; if thrown or jerked either Umpire shall call “No-ball.”

old_text: The Bowler shall deliver the Ball with one foot on the ground behind the bowling crease, and within the return crease, otherwise the Umpire shall call “No Ball.”
new_text: The Bowler shall deliver the Ball with one foot on the ground behind the bowling crease, and within the return crease, otherwise the Umpire shall call “No-Ball.”

old_text: If the Bowler shall bowl the Ball so high over or so wide of the wicket, that, in the opinion of the Umpire, it is not within reach of the Striker, the Umpire shall call “Wide Ball.”
new_text: If the Bowler shall bowl the Ball so high over or so wide of the wicket, that in the opinion of the Umpire, it is not within reach of the Striker, the Umpire shall call “Wide Ball.”

old_text: Neither a “No Ball” nor “Wide Ball” shall be reckoned as one of the “Over.”
new_text: Neither a “No-Ball” nor “Wide Ball” shall be reckoned as one of the “Over.”

old_text: The Striker may hit a “No Ball,” and whatever runs result shall be added to his score: but he shall not be out from a “No Ball,” unless he be run out or break Laws 26, 27, 29, 30.
new_text: The Striker may hit a “No Ball,” and whatever runs result shall be added to his score; but he shall not be out from a “No Ball,” unless he be run out or break Laws 26, 27, 29, 30.

old_text: From a “Wide Ball” as many runs as are run shall be added to the score as “Wide Balls,” and if no run be otherwise obtained one run shall be so added.
new_text: From a “Wide Ball,” as many runs as are run shall be added to the score as “Wide Balls,” and if no run be otherwise obtained one run shall be so added.

old_text: If the ball, not having been called “Wide” or “No Ball,” pass the Striker without touching his bat or person, and any runs be obtained, the Umpire shall call “Bye”; but if the ball touch any part of the Striker’s person (hand excepted) and any run be obtained, the Umpire shall call “Leg Bye,” such runs to be scored “Byes” and “Leg Byes” respectively.
new_text: If the ball, not having been called “Wide” or “No Ball,” pass the Striker without touching his bat, or person, and any runs be obtained, the Umpire shall call “Bye”; but if the ball touch any part of the Striker’s person (hand excepted) and any run be obtained, the Umpire shall call “Leg Bye,” such runs to be scored “Byes” and “Leg Byes” respectively.

old_text: If the wicket be bowled down, even if the ball first touch the Striker’s bat or person;—“Bowled.”
new_text: If the wicket be bowled down, even if the ball first touch the Striker’s bat or person “Bowled.”

old_text: Or, if the ball, from a stroke of the bat or hand, but not the wrist, be held before it touch the ground, although it be hugged to the body of the catcher;—“Caught.”
new_text: Or, if the ball, from a stroke of the bat or hand,* but not the wrist, be held before it touch the ground, although it be hugged to the body of the catcher “Caught.”

old_text: Or, if in playing at the ball, provided it be not touched by the bat or hand, the Striker be out of his ground, and the wicket be put down by the wicket-keeper with the ball, or with hand or arm with ball in hand;—“Stumped.”
new_text: Or, if in playing at the ball, provided it be not touched by the bat or hand, the Striker be out of his ground, and the wicket be put down by the wicket-keeper with the ball, or with hand or arm with ball in hand “Stumped.”

old_text: It is sufficient for the wicket-keeper to remove one bail in order to run out or stump a batsman.
new_text: It's sufficient for the wicket-keeper to remove one bail in order to run out or stump a batsman.

old_text: Or, if with part of his person he stops the ball, which in the opinion of the Umpire at the bowler’s wicket, shall have been pitched in a straight line from it to the Striker’s wicket and would have hit it;—“Leg before wicket.”
new_text: Or, if with part of his person he stops the ball, which in the opinion of the Umpire at the bowler’s wicket, shall have been pitched in a straight line from it to the Striker’s wicket and would have hit it; “Leg before wicket”

old_text: There are three considerations which an Umpire must bear in mind:— (1)
new_text: There are three considerations which an Umpire must bear in mind (1)

old_text: Or, if in playing at the ball he hit down his wicket with his bat or any part of his person or dress;—“Hit Wicket.”
new_text: Or, if in playing at the ball he hit down his wicket with his bat or any part of his person or dress “Hit Wicket.”

old_text: Or, if under pretence of running, or otherwise, either of the batsmen wilfully prevent a ball from being caught;—“Obstructing the field.”
new_text: Or, if under pretence of running, or otherwise, either of the batsmen wilfully prevent a ball from being caught “Obstructing the field.”

old_text: Or, if the ball be struck or be stopped by any part of his person, and he wilfully strike it again, except it be done for the purpose of guarding his wicket, which he may do with his bat, or any part of his person, except his hands;—“Hit the ball twice.”
new_text: Or, if the ball be struck or be stopped by any part of his person, and he wilfully strike it again, except it be done for the purpose of guarding his wicket, which he may do with his bat, or any part of his person, except his hands “Hit the ball twice.”

old_text: The fact that a run is attempted may be evidence of the batsman’s intention to take advantage of the second stroke and the Umpire is entitled to regard it as such, but it is not conclusive.
new_text: The fact, that a run is attempted may be evidence of the batsman’s intention to take advantage of the second stroke and the Umpire is entitled to regard it as such, but it is not conclusive.

old_text: If in running, or at any other time, when the ball is in play he be out of his ground, and his wicket be struck down by the ball after touching any fieldsman, or by the hand or arm, with ball in hand, of any fieldsman; —“Run out.”
new_text: If in running, or at any other time, when the ball is in play he be out of his ground, and his wicket be struck down by the ball as after touching any fieldsman, or by the hand or arm, with ball in hand, of any fieldsman “Run out.”

old_text: Or, if he touch with his hands or take up the ball while in play, unless at the request of the opposite side;—“Handled the ball.”
new_text: Or, if he touch with his hands or take up the ball while in play, unless at the request of the opposite side ;—“Handled the ball.”

old_text: Or, if he wilfully obstruct any Fieldsman;—“Obstructing the field.”
new_text: Or, if he wilfully obstruct any fieldsman ;—“Obstructing the field.”

old_text: If the batsmen have crossed each other, he that runs for the wicket which is put down is out; if they have not crossed he that has left the wicket which is put down is out.
new_text: If the batsmen have crossed each other, he that runs for the wicket which is put down is out ; if they have not crossed he that has left the wicket which is put down is out.

old_text: When a run has been made oft’ a no-ball the no-ball should be scored although the ball has been caught.
new_text: When a run has been made off a no-ball the no-ball should be scored although the ball has been caught. 12

old_text: If a ball in play cannot be found or recovered, any Fieldsman may call “Lost Ball,” when the ball shall be “Dead”; six runs shall be added to the score; but if more than six runs have boon run before “Lost Ball” has been called, as many runs as have been run shall be scored.
new_text: If a ball in play cannot be found or recovered, any Fieldsman may call “Lost Ball,” when the ball shall be “Dead” ; six runs shall be added to the score ; but if more than six runs have been run before “Lost Ball” has been called, as many runs as have been run shall be scored.

old_text: After the ball shall have been finally settled in the Wicketkeeper’s or Bowler’s hand, it shall be “Dead”; but when the Bowler is about to deliver the ball, if the Batsman at his wicket be out of his ground before actual delivery, the said Bowler may run him out; but if the Bowler throw at that wicket and any run result, it shall be scored “No Ball.”
new_text: After the ball shall have been finally settled in the Wicketkeeper’s or Bowler’s hand, it shall be “Dead” ; but when the Bowler is about to deliver the ball, if the Batsman at his wicket be out of his ground before actual delivery, the said Bowler may run him out; but if the Bowler throw at that wicket and any run result, it shall be scored “No Ball.”

old_text: He may have passed the bowling crease in his run or may change the ball from one hand to the other before throwing at the wicket or knocking oft’ the bails.
new_text: He may have passed the bowling crease in his run or may change the ball from one hand to the other before throwing at the wicket or knocking off the bails.

old_text: A substitute shall be allowed to field or run between wickets for any player, who may during the match, be incapacitated from illness or injury, but for no other reason, except with the consent of the opposite side
new_text: A substitute shall be allowed to field or run between wickets for any player, who may during the match, be incapacitated from illness or injury, but for no other reason, except with the consent of the opposite side. 13

old_text: Many disputes would be avoided if the Captains, before tossing, exchanged lists of the players.
new_text: Many disputes would be avoided if the Captains, before tossing exchanged lists of the players.

old_text: In case any substitute shall be allowed to run between wickets, the Striker may bo run out if either he or his substitute be out of his ground.
new_text: In case any substitute shall be allowed to run between wickets, the Striker may be run out if either he or his substitute be out of his ground.

old_text: When the injured Batsman is not the Striker he is subject to no penalty under this Law.
new_text: When the injured Batsman is not the Striker he is subject only to such penalty under this Law as is incurred by his runner.

word_diff.new: Law as is incurred by his runner.

old_text: A Batsman is liable to be out for any infringement of the Laws by his substitute.
new_text: A Batsman is liable to be out for any infringment of the Laws by his substitute.

old_text: If he shall take the ball for the purpose of stumping, before it has passed the wicket, or, if he shall incommode the Striker by any noise, or motion, or if any part of his person be over or before the wicket, the Striker shall not be out, excepting under Laws 26, 27, 28, 29, and 30.
new_text: If he shall take the ball for the purpose of stumping, before it has passed the wicket, or, if he shall incommode the Striker by any noise, or motion, or if any part of his person be over or before the wicket, the Striker shall not be out, excepting under Laws 26, 27, 28, 29 and 30.

old_text: The Umpires are the sole judges of fair or unfair play, of the fitness of the ground, the weather, and the light for play; all disputes, shall be determined by them, and if they disagree the actual state of things shall continue.
new_text: The Umpires are the sole judges of fair or unfair play, of the fitness of the ground, the weather, and the light for play ; all disputes shall be determined by them, and if they disagree the actual state of things shall continue.

old_text: The In-going Batsman should meet the out-coming batsman before he enters the Pavilion..
new_text: The In-going Batsman should meet the out-coming batsman before he enters the Pavilion.

old_text: The Umpires shall take especial care to call “No Ball” instantly upon delivery; “Wide Ball” as soon as it shall have passed the striker.
new_text: The Umpire shall take especial care to call “No Ball” instantly upon delivery; “Wide Ball” as soon as it shall have passed the striker.

old_text: No act on the part of the fielding side can cause a batsman to be out after the Umpire has called “Over,” but an appeal may be made within the allotted time.
new_text: No act on the part of the fielding side can cause a batsman to be out after the Umpire has called “Over,” but an appeal may be made within the allotted time. 15

old_text: The In-side may declare their innings at an end in a three days’ match, at any time on the second day; in a two days’ match the Captain of the batting side has power to declare his innings at a close at any time; but such declaration may not be made on the first day later than 1 hour and 40 minutes before the hour agreed on for drawing stumps; in a one day match at any time.
new_text: The In-side may declare their innings at an end in a three days’ match, at any time on the second day ; in a two days’ match the Captain of the batting side has power to declare his innings at a close at any time ; but such declaration may not be made on the first day later than 1 hour and 40 minutes before the hour agreed on for drawing stumps ; in a one day match at any time.

old_text: Prior to the commencement of a match it may be agreed:—that the Over consist of 5 or 6 balls.
new_text: Prior to the commencement of a match it may be agreed :—that the Over consist of 5 or 6 balls.

old_text: When there shall be less than five players on a side, Bounds shall be placed twenty-two yards each in a line from the off and leg stump.
new_text: When there shall be less than five players on a side, Bounds shall be placed twenty-two yards each in a line from the off and leg stump. 16

old_text: When there shall he less than five players on a side, neither Byes, Leg Byes, nor Overthrows shall be allowed, nor shall the Striker be caught out behind the wicket, nor stumped.
new_text: When there shall be less than five players on a side, neither Byes, Leg Byes, nor Overthrows shall be allowed, nor shall the Striker be caught out behind the wicket, nor stumped.

old_text: The fieldsman must return the ball so that it shall cross the ground between the wicket and the bowling stump, or between the bowling stump and the bounds; the Striker may run till the ball be so returned.
new_text: The fieldsman must return the ball so that it shall cross the ground between the wicket and the bowling stump, or between the bowling stump and the bounds ; the Striker may run till the ball be so returned.

old_text: When there shall be more than four players on a side, there shall he no bounds.
new_text: When there shall be more than four players on a side, there shall be no bounds.
